reflux_tier_why: Unchanged from design/05: middling reflux per essence, but lightning reflux does not shed in a fight except by Overloading (each grounds 12). Finish targets or seize up.
rule: Lightning marks a target and overloads it: every lightning hit leaves Live marks, and the third mark is an Overload that stuns the target and arcs to every other marked enemy within 12 m.
_note: DRAFT 2026-10-22 [MODEL]. Lightning is in the game: existing skills keep their runes (runes.json skill_anchor); Arc Lash, Thunderclap Palm and Stepped Leader carry Brent's approved changes; Stored Bolt is design/05's L6, not yet built. Four new skills fill the runes that had none (Strike, Insulate, Stun, Silence). Arc and Charge carry a second skill, allowed because every lightning rune now has one. Lightning's rune effects already exist in runes.json, so 'effects' is empty. Field names follow abilities.json; new keys are named in new_mechanics.

skills.name: Plumb Bolt
skills.summary: One enemy within 14 m is struck from straight above: 100 damage, 30 poise and a Live mark. Bodies, shields and low walls between you do not stop it.
skills.verb_fit: Strike is 'a bolt that hits one target'. This is that bolt with nothing added: one body, from the sky, no line to block and no jump. Every other lightning skill either travels a line or spreads; this one only lands.

new_mechanics.name: smite
new_mechanics.definition: kind 'smite': an instant hit on the enemy under the cursor (or your locked target) within 'range', no travel and no wind-up; checked before essence is spent. With 'from_above' nothing between you and it blocks it and a frontal block (front_armour, blocks_shots) does not apply.

good_modifiers.word: A charged strike: two marks from one bolt, so Plumb Bolt then Arc Lash is an Overload on someone 14 m away.
Thunder after the strike: the crack Dazes the target and knocks 30% more poise out of it.
Everything into one body, which is Strike's own nature said twice: +25% damage.
A plumb line from higher up: reach 19.6 m, a little weaker.
Drive it into a body already marked: +40% against Live targets, so it finishes what Arc Lash started.

bad_modifiers.why: Plumb Bolt is the one lightning skill that does not jump, and the jump op only works on a chain; Arc falls back to a sliver of damage.
There is no shot to pass through bodies; it already ignores what is between. Falls back to a sliver of damage.
Nothing of a bolt stays to be made longer. No duration field; falls back.

skills.name: Ground Rod
skills.summary: Point, 8 m: a rod for 10 s that blocks nothing. Each lightning skill you cast within 8 m of it also arcs from the rod to the nearest enemy within 5 m: 40 and a mark. One rod at a time.
skills.verb_fit: Ground is 'earth a charge away; draw strikes to a point'. The rod is that point: your casts near it are drawn down through it to a second target, and it leaves little reflux behind.

good_modifiers.word: A rod that stays: 15 s instead of 10.
A charged rod: each relay leaves two marks, so the rod finishes what your cast started.
A taller rod: set farther away, listens and reaches farther.
The rod's arc hits marked bodies 40% harder.

bad_modifiers.why: A rod is a place; there is no flight or dash to speed up. Falls back to a little damage.
No wind-up and no speed to quicken; a rod that stands is already instant. Falls back.
Nothing it throws to pass through bodies. Falls back.

skills.name: Static Coat
skills.summary: 6 s: an enemy that hits you in melee takes 25 and a Live mark, and every second bare strike you land adds a mark.
skills.verb_fit: Charge is 'build up marks'. The coat builds them without a cast: every exchange in melee, theirs or yours, charges the bodies around you.

good_modifiers.word: A coat that holds its charge: 9 s.
Worn closer: lasts 30% longer.
An angry coat: the retaliation bites 20% harder, for a little more essence.

bad_modifiers.why: A coat is worn, not thrown: it has no range or area, so all that lands is Far's small damage cut on the retaliation.
A coat worn somewhere else is not worn. No reach to move; falls back.
Nothing it shoots. Falls back.

skills.name: Stored Bolt
skills.summary: Hold up to 1.2 s, walking slowly; let go for an instant line 12 m long through everything: 100 to 300 damage and 1 to 3 Live marks by how long you held. A full charge Overloads the whole line.
skills.verb_fit: Charge is 'build up marks'. The hold is the charge, measured in marks: one, two, three.

good_modifiers.word: A longer line: 16.8 m.
Grounded while you hold it: the release leaves 25% less reflux.
design/05's Compression: a thinner, denser line, shorter but 25% harder.

bad_modifiers.why: It already passes through everything on the line, and it is not a shot. Falls back.
A line through everything has nothing left to jump to, and the jump op needs a chain. Falls back.
It reads well (release the stored marks) but Charge and Discharge are opposites with an ionic bond (2.74 vs 1.0): Charge keeps all the pull and Discharge adds nothing at all.

skills.name: Dead Short
skills.summary: Every marked enemy within 12 m Overloads now: 40% of the full blow and stun at 1 mark, 70% at 2, all of it at 3. It grounds no reflux.
skills.verb_fit: Discharge is 'release them as an overload'. This releases every mark in the room at once, at a discount for the ones not yet full.

good_modifiers.word: design/05's Reach: the short finds marks out to 15.6 m.
Carried on clean essence: 15% cheaper, which matters on a dear panic button.
A grounded short: it still grounds nothing itself, but leaves 25% less reflux.

bad_modifiers.why: Charge is Discharge's opposite and the bond is ionic (2.74 vs 1.0): Charge takes the whole pull, and Dead Short has no hit for a mark to ride on. Falls back.
An insulated short does not short. The bond is ionic (2.95 vs 1.0), so Insulate takes the pull and all it adds is a cost cut.
Nothing it shoots. Falls back.

skills.name: Arc Lash
skills.summary: Instant and short: it cannot miss what it points at. 85 damage and a Live mark, then it arcs to one more enemy within 4 m for the same. Walls stop it.
skills.verb_fit: Arc is 'jump between targets'. Brent's ruling: built on Arc, it must jump. It now leaves the first body for the next one.

new_mechanics.name: beam jumps
new_mechanics.definition: A beam may carry 'jumps' and 'jump_radius': after the first enemy it hits, the payload jumps to the nearest not-yet-hit enemy within jump_radius, as a chain does. (effects_v1 only lets 'jumps +n' act on kind chain; it should read the jumps field instead.)

good_modifiers.word: A charged lash: two marks on each body, so two lashes Overload two enemies.
The lash hits marked bodies 40% harder: the finisher of a mark you laid.
design/05's Reach: 12.6 m, and the jump reaches farther.
A tight, hot lash: shorter range and jump, 25% harder.

bad_modifiers.why: Insulate is Arc's opposite and pulls harder (2.95 vs 2.15, polar): Arc's hold on the skill is halved (its single jump survives only by rounding), and all Insulate adds is a cost cut. Blocking the jump the skill is built on.
A beam is not a shot to pierce with; it already hits what it touches. Falls back.
Nothing of an instant beam lasts. No duration; falls back.

skills.name: Forked Path
skills.summary: One enemy within 9 m, then up to three more within 5 m of each other: 50 and 1 Live mark each. Never the same body twice.
skills.verb_fit: Arc is 'jump between targets'. Forked Path is nothing but jumps: it primes the room for an Overload without finishing anyone.

good_modifiers.word: One more road: a fourth jump, each a little lighter.
design/05's Reach: farther to the first body and farther between them.
Each fork hits marked bodies 40% harder, so it can follow an Overload's arc.
A wider net: longer jumps, lighter touches.

bad_modifiers.why: Insulate is Arc's opposite and pulls harder (polar): the jumps are halved, which is the whole skill. All it adds is a cost cut.
Not a shot. Falls back.
No duration field. (The design/05 idea, marks lasting 14 s, needs a status-duration group the effect system does not have.)

skills.name: Bell Jar
skills.summary: One enemy within 12 m is sealed under a jar of still air for 6 s: 30 damage and a Live mark. Nothing passes in or out of it: no auras, no death burst, no arcs. Overload it and the whole arc stays inside: +60 for every other marked enemy within 12 m.
skills.verb_fit: Insulate is 'block a jump, isolate a target'. The jar is both: the room's arcs cannot reach it or leave it, and the enemy is cut off from its own side.

new_mechanics.name: insulated
new_mechanics.definition: 1 stack, 'duration' seconds. Nothing passes into or out of the target: allies' auras (drummed, a Censer-Bearer's burst) skip it, its own aura and death burst go nowhere, Overload arcs and Soaked conduction skip it. An Overload on it does not arc out; it takes +arc_damage (60) for every other marked enemy within arc_radius instead, and those keep their marks.

good_modifiers.word: Two marks under the jar: one Thunderclap Palm Overloads it, alone and with the whole arc inside.
The seal holds 9 s.
Seal a Censer-Bearer at the back of the room: 16.8 m.
A grounded jar: the cast leaves less reflux behind.

bad_modifiers.why: Arc is the jump the jar exists to block, and the jump op needs a chain. Falls back to a sliver of damage.
A jar has no wind-up and no flight to quicken. Falls back.
Not a shot. Falls back.

skills.name: Stepped Leader
skills.summary: You are simply there, up to 6 m away: over enemies and gaps, not through walls or stone. A Live mark on everything beside where you land, and you are Quickened for 2 s after.
skills.verb_fit: Quicken is 'nerves in overdrive'. The blink is the fastest movement in the game, and the approved change carries the overdrive on past the landing.

new_mechanics.name: quickened
new_mechanics.definition: On the player, 2 s: move 20% faster and every recovery (skill, strike, dash) is 30% shorter. Re-applying refreshes.

good_modifiers.word: design/05's Reach: about 8 m, and the landing marks a wider ring.
Land charged: two marks on everything beside you.
Out of the blink even sooner: recovery 25% shorter.

bad_modifiers.why: A blink held in place is not a blink. No duration, and slowing an instant does nothing; falls back.
Nothing to pierce. Falls back.
Nothing of the blink stays. (Quickened's 2 s is not in a stat group.) Falls back.

skills.name: Seize Up
skills.summary: Everything within 3 m locks up: 30 damage, and Stunned for 0.4 s for every Live mark it carries (0.2 s if none). It spends no marks.
skills.verb_fit: Stun is 'nerves locked'. The lock lasts by how much charge is already in them, so it reads lightning's marks without cashing them in: Dead Short spends marks for a partial Overload; this keeps them for the Palm that follows.

new_mechanics.name: stun by marks
new_mechanics.definition: A payload with 'stun_per_mark' sets Stunned to stun_per_mark x the target's Live marks (stun_min if none), read before any mark the hit adds; 'elite_stun_mult' scales it on elites.

good_modifiers.word: Lock and charge: a mark on everything it locks, so a marked crowd is one touch from Overloading.
A wider seizure, a little weaker: 3.9 m.
The lock comes with a crack: Dazed and 30% more poise lost.

bad_modifiers.why: Quicken is Stun's opposite: nerves in overdrive do not lock. Stun keeps the pull, and there is no wind-up or flight to quicken; falls back.
Not a shot. Falls back.
The lock is a moment; there is no duration field to stretch. Falls back.

skills.name: Thunderclap Palm
skills.summary: One enemy in reach: a heavy blow, 2 Live marks, and it stops whatever it was doing. The crack Dazes and staggers everyone within 2.5 m of it, the target too.
skills.verb_fit: Thunder is 'a deafening crack that staggers'. The approved change makes the Palm do exactly that: the blow is the bolt, the crack around it is the thunder.

new_mechanics.name: burst statuses
new_mechanics.definition: A targeted_strike's 'burst' (exists for Kiln Fist) may carry 'statuses', applied to every enemy within burst_radius of the target, the target included.

good_modifiers.word: design/05's held Palm: three marks, so the Palm alone Overloads.
A louder crack: reach and the 2.5 m ring grow 30%, the blow 10% lighter.
Palm a marked body for 40% more: the closer after Arc Lash.

bad_modifiers.why: Silence is Thunder's opposite and pulls harder (3.25 vs 2.01): a silent thunderclap. Its only op, interrupts, is already on the Palm; falls back.
Not a shot. Falls back.
A blow has no duration. Falls back.

skills.name: Dead Line
skills.summary: Point, 9 m: a ring 3 m across hums for 6 s. Enemies inside cannot cast, drum or call for help. Each is interrupted and takes a Live mark once, on entering.
skills.verb_fit: Silence is 'dead quiet: casting and calls fail'. The ring is a dead line: nothing said inside it gets out, and what was being said is cut off.

new_mechanics.name: muted
new_mechanics.definition: 1 stack, 1 s, refreshed while inside: cannot cast, start a drum roll or a Wall Commander's call, or send the reinforcements signal. Plain attacks still land.

new_mechanics.name: zone on_enter
new_mechanics.definition: A ground_zone's 'on_enter' payload is applied once to each enemy, when it is first inside (at the cast, or when it walks in); 'payload' is applied every tick.

good_modifiers.word: A longer silence: 9 s.
Drop the line on the Drummer at the back: reach and ring 30% larger.
A field that leaks nothing costs 15% less.

bad_modifiers.why: The maths would accept it (the zone has a payload) but the payload ticks every 0.5 s: a mark per tick is an Overload machine, not a ring of silence. Marks belong on on_enter, which the effect system does not reach.
Thunder is Silence's opposite: a crack inside a hush undoes it. The maths would Daze everything inside every tick.
Not a shot. Falls back.
